Define a ctsem model

Source: R/ctModel.R
ctModel.Rd

Specifies a continuous or discrete time dynamic model, to be fitted with ctFit or used to generate data with ctGenerate.

Usage

ctModel(
  LAMBDA,
  type = "ct",
  n.manifest = "auto",
  n.latent = "auto",
  Tpoints = NULL,
  manifestNames = "auto",
  manifesttype = rep(0, nrow(LAMBDA)),
  ncategories = NULL,
  censormin = NULL,
  censormax = NULL,
  latentNames = "auto",
  id = "id",
  time = "time",
  silent = FALSE,
  T0VAR = "auto",
  T0MEANS = "auto",
  MANIFESTMEANS = "auto",
  MANIFESTVAR = "diag",
  ASYMPTOTES = NA,
  RESPONSE = NA,
  WIENER = NA,
  DRIFT = "auto",
  CINT = 0,
  DIFFUSION = "auto",
  n.TDpred = "auto",
  TDpredNames = "auto",
  TDPREDEFFECT = "auto",
  TDPREDMEANS = "auto",
  TDPREDVAR = "auto",
  n.TIpred = "auto",
  TIpredNames = "auto",
  tipredDefault = TRUE,
  PARS = NULL,
  driftScaled = character()
)

Arguments

LAMBDA

n.manifest*n.latent loading matrix relating latent to manifest variables, with latent processes 1:n.latent along the columns, and manifest variables 1:n.manifest in the rows.

type

character string. Use 'ct' (continuous time) or 'dt' (discrete time) for fitting with ctFit. These return a modern ctsem model object whose pars data frame can also be edited through the pars-backed matrices view. For legacy workflows, 'omx' returns a matrix-list model object that can be edited directly and then converted via ctModelConvertOMX.

n.manifest

Number of manifest indicators per individual at each measurement occasion / time point. Manifest variables are included as the first element of the wide data matrix, with all the 1:n.manifest manifest variables at time 1 followed by those of time 2, and so on.

n.latent

Number of latent processes.

Tpoints

Number of time points, or measurement occasions, in the data. This will generally be the maximum number of time points for a single individual, but may be one extra if sample relative time intervals are used, see ctIntervalise.

manifestNames

n.manifest length vector of manifest variable names as they appear in the data structure, without any _Tx time point suffix that may be present in wide data. Defaults to Y1, Y2, etc.

manifesttype

n.manifest length vector of manifest variable types: 0 (the default) for continuous Gaussian variables, 1 for binary (coded 0/1), 2 for ordinal (consecutive integers from 1), 3 for counts (non-negative integers, Poisson with a log link, so the latent process gives the log rate) 4 for censored (Gaussian, observed between censormin and censormax) and 5 for choice and response time. For a count the MANIFESTVAR diagonal stays free and is a log-scale dispersion, giving a Poisson-lognormal observation with variance \(\mu + \mu^2(e^{\sigma^2}-1)\). Fix it to zero for a plain Poisson. A censored value at a limit contributes the probability of being at or beyond that limit. A choice and response time variable holds the response time in seconds, negative for a response at the lower boundary, and follows the drift diffusion model: its linear predictor is the drift, its MANIFESTVAR diagonal the trial to trial standard deviation of the drift, and WIENER sets the rest. Types other than 0 need the julia backend, except binary, which stan also fits.

ncategories

n.manifest length integer vector giving the number of categories of each ordinal manifest variable, ignored for other types. Required when any manifesttype is 2, by ctGenerate as well as ctFit.

censormin, censormax

n.manifest length numeric vectors giving the lower and upper censoring limits of each manifesttype = 4 variable, ignored for other types. The defaults are -Inf and Inf, so a variable censored on one side keeps the other limit infinite. The limits are fixed, known values.

latentNames

n.latent length vector of latent variable names (used for naming parameters, defaults to eta1, eta2, etc).

id

character string denoting column name containing subject identification variables. id data may be of any form, though will be coerced internally to an integer sequence rising from 1. Or a character vector of column names for nested grouping levels, innermost first: id = c('subject','study') places each subject in one study. The indvarying field of a cell (see ctPar) sets the levels its parameter varies at: TRUE for every level, FALSE for none, or the names of levels. For example 'cint||study' gives an intercept that varies between studies, and 'cint||subject,study' (or TRUE) one that varies at both levels. model$pars$indvarying holds these values, one per cell, and can be edited directly. A cell's sdscale applies at every level it varies at. Intercepts (T0MEANS, MANIFESTMEANS, CINT) that are left unspecified vary at every level. Levels above the subject require backend='julia' with intoverpop='laplace', and the levels must be strictly nested.

time

character string denoting column name containing timing data. Timing data must be numeric.

silent

Suppress all output to console.

T0VAR

lower triangular n.latent*n.latent matrix of latent process initial variance / covariance, with standard deviations on the diagonal and covariance parameters below it (see ctCov). Under the default covmattransform, 'z', a cell below the diagonal fixed to 0 gives a covariance of zero. "auto" freely estimates all parameters.

T0MEANS

n.latent*1 matrix of latent process means at first time point, T0. "auto" freely estimates all parameters.

MANIFESTMEANS

n.manifest*1 matrix of manifest intercept parameters. "auto" frees all parameters.

MANIFESTVAR

lower triangular n.manifest*n.manifest matrix of variance / covariance between manifests at each measurement occasion (i.e. measurement error / residual), with standard deviations on the diagonal and covariance parameters below it (see ctCov). Under the default covmattransform, 'z', a cell below the diagonal fixed to 0 gives a covariance of zero. "auto" freely estimates variance parameters, and fixes covariances between manifests to 0. "free" frees all values, including covariances.

ASYMPTOTES

Matrix with one row per binary indicator, in manifest order, and two columns giving the lower and upper asymptotes of its response probability. The probability is then lower + (upper - lower) times the logistic of the linear predictor. NA means no asymptote on that side, and the default of all NA gives the two parameter logistic model. A parameter name in the lower column estimates a guessing probability (three parameter model), in the upper column a ceiling below one, and in both the four parameter model. A number between 0 and 1 fixes the asymptote, and a name repeated across rows estimates one asymptote for those items. A length 2 vector applies to every binary indicator, so c('guess', NA) estimates one guessing parameter for the whole test. Julia backend only.

RESPONSE

Matrix with one row per manifest variable and two columns, setting the response scale of censored indicators (manifesttype 4). Rows for other indicators keep their defaults. Column 1, halfwidth, is half the width of the interval a recorded value stands for. A value y means the latent response lies between the transformed y - halfwidth and y + halfwidth, a value at censormin that it lies below censormin + halfwidth, and a value at censormax that it lies above censormax - halfwidth. The default, 0, treats values as exact. For a rating scale use half the step between categories. A step that differs between studies can be written as a time independent predictor in the cell. Column 2, power, sets the transform from the recorded scale to the latent response, \(G(r) = L + ((1 + r - L)^p - 1)/p\), with \(L\) the censormin (0 if there is none). The default, 1, is linear. Values below 1 make the latent response change less per recorded unit towards the top of the scale, and 0 gives the log transform. A parameter name estimates the power, and a name shared across items or studies estimates one power from all of them. NA keeps the default, and a length 2 vector fills every censored row, so c(0.5, 'power') suits integer data with one estimated transform. Julia backend only.

WIENER

Matrix with one row per manifest variable and three columns, the boundary separation, nondecision time (seconds) and relative start point (as a proportion of the boundary separation, from the lower boundary) of choice and response time indicators (manifesttype 5). Rows for other indicators are not used. The default estimates the boundary and nondecision time and fixes the start at 0.5. Cells take parameter names, values, random effects and time dependent predictors as other matrices do, so 'a * exp(b_speed * speed)' lets the boundary change with a speed instruction. NA keeps a default, and a length 3 vector fills every choice and response time row. Julia backend only.

DRIFT

n.latent*n.latent matrix of drift coefficients: auto effects on the diagonal and cross effects off it. The cell in row i and column j is the effect of process j on the rate of change of process i, per unit of time. A negative auto effect makes a process on its own return to its equilibrium after a shock. Whether the processes together are stable depends on the whole matrix. They are stable when every eigenvalue has a negative real part, which negative auto effects alone do not ensure. ctDiscretePars gives the effects over a time interval. With type = 'dt', the autoregressive and cross-lagged coefficients from one occasion to the next. "auto" frees every cell, with the auto effects bounded below zero in continuous time.

CINT

n.latent * 1 matrix of continuous time intercepts. With a stable drift matrix the processes settle at -solve(DRIFT, CINT). Fixed to zero by default, with the levels in MANIFESTMEANS instead. Free it for trends, or for individual differences in the equilibrium. A process and its first indicator share one level, so free only one of its CINT and that indicator's MANIFESTMEANS.

DIFFUSION

lower triangular n.latent*n.latent matrix of diffusion process variance and covariance (latent error / dynamic innovation), with standard deviations on the diagonal and covariance parameters below it (see ctCov). Under the default covmattransform, 'z', a cell below the diagonal fixed to 0 gives a covariance of zero. "auto" freely estimates all parameters.

n.TDpred

Number of time dependent predictor variables in the dataset.

TDpredNames

n.TDpred length vector of time dependent predictor variable names, as they appear in the data structure, without any _Tx time point suffix that may appear in wide data. Default names are TD1, TD2, etc.

TDPREDEFFECT

n.latent*n.TDpred matrix of effects from time dependent predictors to latent processes. Effects from 1:n.TDpred columns TDpredictors go to 1:n.latent rows of latent processes. A predictor acts as an impulse: at each row the processes shift by its value times its effects, and the dynamics carry the shift forward. Effects that last or build up are modelled with an extra latent process, see vignette('interventions'). "auto" freely estimates all parameters.

TDPREDMEANS

Legacy argument for time-dependent predictor means, mainly to support data generation workflows. Expected dimensions are (n.TDpred * Tpoints) rows and 1 column. "auto" creates a free-label matrix.

TDPREDVAR

Legacy argument for time-dependent predictor covariance structure, mainly to support data generation workflows. Expected dimensions are (n.TDpred * Tpoints) square. "auto" creates a free-label matrix.

n.TIpred

Number of time independent predictors. Each TIpredictor is inserted at the right of the data matrix, after the time intervals.

TIpredNames

n.TIpred length vector of time independent predictor variable names, as they appear in the data structure. Default names are TI1, TI2, etc. Or a formula of such names and smooth terms, such as ~ s(age, k = 8) + female. A smooth term is a penalised spline of a subject-level covariate, with its smoothness estimated from the data (backend = 'julia'). It enters the model as k - 1 predictor columns, age_lin (the linear trend) and age_s1, ..., built from the data when the model is fitted. To give a parameter the smooth effect, name the covariate in its cell's tipreds field ('cint||||age'). Under tipredDefault = TRUE, cells without a tipreds field get the smooth effect if their parameter is free and varies between subjects.

tipredDefault

Logical. TRUE sets any parameters with unspecified time independent predictor effects to have effects estimated, FALSE fixes the effect to zero unless individually specified. A cell's effects are unspecified only when its tipreds field is left out. An empty field ('mypar||||') means no predictor effects, which excludes a parameter under tipredDefault = TRUE. The setting is stored on the model as $tipredDefault.

PARS

for types 'ct' and 'dt' only. May be of any structure, only needed to contain extra parameters for certain non-linear models.

driftScaled

for type 'ct' only: which of "DIFFUSION" and "CINT" to parameterise by what they add over one time unit, given the process's own drift diagonal a. A diffusion sd s becomes s * sqrt(2 a / expm1(2 a)), so that s^2 is the variance the process gains from its own noise over one time unit. An intercept u becomes u * a / expm1(a). The model and its likelihood are unchanged. The rescaled parameters depend less on the drift diagonal, which helps uncertainty estimation and sampling when fast mean reversion and larger noise are hard to tell apart. Only the diagonal of DIFFUSION is rescaled, so its correlations keep their usual meaning. Each rescaled parameter, with its name, transform, random effects and predictor effects, moves to a new cell of PARS, and its original cell becomes an expression of that cell and the drift diagonal. Not available with covmattransform = 'cholesky'.

Value

For type = 'ct' or 'dt', a model of class ctStanModel, with one row per matrix cell in $pars and the same cells as matrices in $matrices. Either can be edited. For type = 'omx', a list of matrices of class ctsemInit, for ctGenerate or ctModelConvertOMX.

Details

In continuous time (type = 'ct') the latent processes \(\eta(t)\) of each subject follow $$d\eta(t) = (A \eta(t) + b + M \chi(t)) dt + G dW(t)$$ and are measured as $$y(t) = \Lambda \eta(t) + \tau + \epsilon(t)$$ Here \(A\) is DRIFT, \(b\) is CINT, \(M\) is TDPREDEFFECT, \(\chi(t)\) the time dependent predictors, \(GG^\top\) is the covariance of the random shocks, given by DIFFUSION, \(\Lambda\) is LAMBDA, \(\tau\) is MANIFESTMEANS, and the residuals \(\epsilon(t)\) have the covariance given by MANIFESTVAR. The processes start at T0MEANS, with covariance T0VAR. In discrete time (type = 'dt') the same matrices describe a vector autoregression, with DRIFT holding the autoregressive and cross-lagged coefficients from one occasion to the next.

Any matrix not given takes a default: DRIFT, DIFFUSION, TDPREDEFFECT, T0MEANS, T0VAR, MANIFESTMEANS and the diagonal of MANIFESTVAR are free, CINT is zero, and T0MEANS and MANIFESTMEANS vary over subjects. Printing the model shows every cell. vignette('ctsem') works through a first analysis, and vignette('dynamics') explains how to read the drift matrix.

A matrix cell can be one of four things:

  • a number, which fixes the cell;

  • a parameter name, which frees it. The same name in two cells is one parameter, which is how equality constraints are written;

  • a name with fields, giving the transform, the levels of id at which the parameter varies, the prior scale of that variation, and the time independent predictors that affect it;

  • an expression, computed from the latent states, the time dependent predictors and the PARS cells.

Fields can be given in a fixed order separated by | ('mm||TRUE|0.5'), or by name ('mm, indvarying=TRUE, sdscale=0.5'). With nested ids, indvarying may name levels, as in 'mm||study' or 'mm, indvarying=c(subject, study)'. A cell containing | is read in the ordered form. Otherwise a cell with a field of the form name=value is read in the named form, and an unknown field name is an error. ctPar writes these strings from named arguments.

Every name in an expression must be a latent state, a time dependent predictor, or a parameter declared in PARS. For example DRIFT = matrix('-exp(dr)*eta1') needs PARS = c('dr'). To transform a single parameter, the transform field is shorter: DRIFT = matrix('dr|-exp(param)'). With the julia backend a cell may also use a time independent predictor by name, which gives the subject's value of it, as in MANIFESTVAR = 'rsd + mvar' with PARS = c('mvar|1e-10 + 5 * log1p_exp(2 * param)'). Missing values of such a predictor are imputed or sampled like other missing predictor values (optimcontrol$tipredMissing). Population summaries evaluate the cell at a predictor value of zero. A cell cannot refer to a manifest variable or to the time interval. Predictor effects on a parameter are set with the tipreds field.

A latent state or time dependent predictor name in a cell refers to that state or predictor, and any number of matrices may refer to the same one. A name declared in PARS likewise refers to the PARS cell wherever else it appears, and that cell holds the parameter and its transform.

Any other name repeated across cells is one parameter, with one value and one random effect, so it needs one transform. Cells that would transform it differently are refused, including cells whose default transforms differ. The DRIFT diagonal is bounded negative and the off-diagonals are not, so DRIFT = matrix('a', 2, 2) is refused. To use one parameter in cells that need different transforms, declare it in PARS (PARS = c('a')) and write the transform in each cell, as in DRIFT[1,1] = '-exp(a)' and DIFFUSION[1,1] = 'exp(a)'. If one transform suits every cell, give it in PARS (PARS = c('a|-exp(param)')) and write only the name in each cell. Two PARS cells with the same name are one parameter and must have the same transform.

A predictor effect belongs to the parameter, so cells holding one parameter must have the same tipreds. Naming an effect ('mypar||||age=shared') gives every parameter with that effect name, for that predictor, one shared coefficient. Because the coefficient acts on the raw scale, parameters with different transforms cannot share it. The same effect name under two predictors gives two coefficients. A number instead of a name ('mypar||||age=0.5') fixes the effect, shifting each subject's raw parameter value by 0.5 times their age before the transform. Fixed effects are fitted by backend = 'julia' and used by ctGenerate. The stan backend refuses them.

A cell that is exactly a latent state or time dependent predictor name is read as a reference to it, with a warning, since a parameter of that name would give a different model. Write 'state[1]' or 'tdpreds[rowi, 1]' to avoid the warning. In PARS such a cell is an error, because a bare name there declares a parameter. For a PARS cell that depends on a state, write the state in an expression, such as 'log1p(exp(eta1))'.

See also

ctPar for the fields a matrix cell can carry, ctFit for fitting the result.

Examples

# Two processes, each measured by one variable. Everything not given
# takes a default, which printing the model shows.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(2),
  manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'), latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'))
model

# A number fixes a cell and a name frees it. The same name in two cells
# gives one parameter. Here eta1 affects eta2 but not the reverse, and the
# two auto effects are equal.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(2),
  manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'), latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'),
  DRIFT = matrix(c('a',     0,
                   'cross', 'a'), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE))
model$pars[model$pars$matrix %in% 'DRIFT', c('row', 'col', 'param', 'value')]

# One process measured by three indicators, with a time dependent predictor
# (an intervention) acting on it, and a time independent predictor (age)
# affecting its auto effect only.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = matrix(c(1, 'lambda2', 'lambda3'), 3, 1),
  manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2', 'Y3'), latentNames = 'eta',
  TDpredNames = 'treatment', TIpredNames = 'age', tipredDefault = FALSE,
  DRIFT = 'drift_eta, tipreds=c(age)')

# A random effect: the auto effect varies between subjects.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(1), manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta',
  DRIFT = ctPar('drift_eta', indvarying = TRUE))

# A discrete time cross-lagged panel model.
model <- ctModel(type = 'dt', LAMBDA = diag(2),
  manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'), latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'))
